question: A lesion causing compression of the facial nerve at the stylomastoid foramen will cause ipsilateral

options.B: paralysis of the facial muscles and loss of taste.
options.C: paralysis of the facial muscles, loss of taste and lacrimation.
options.D: paralysis of the facial muscles, loss of taste, lacrimation and decreased salivation.

passages.title: Facial nerve anatomy
passages.content: The facial nerve exits the skull through the stylomastoid foramen and then supplies the muscles of facial expression.

passages.title: Taste fibers
passages.content: Taste fibers from the anterior tongue travel through the chorda tympani before joining the facial nerve proximal to the stylomastoid foramen.
